stories.title: GATE 2027 exam schedule announced
stories.summary: IIT Madras will conduct the GATE 2027 exam on February 6, 7, 13, 14, 20, and 21. Official registration and attendance data will be published on the exam website. In 2026, 10,11,719 students registered for the test, with 7,97,434 candidates appearing. The final count remains pending.

stories.title: International graduates projected to generate 1.7 trillion dollars
stories.summary: A study by Studyportals and Cambridge suggests international students who graduated in 2024 will contribute 1.7 trillion dollars to host economies over their working lives. The US, UK, Canada, and Australia are expected to capture 60 percent of this value. Most previous research focused only on spending during studies.

stories.title: TAFE qualifications offer diverse career pathways
stories.summary: TAFE courses provide training for hundreds of roles beyond traditional trades. For example, TAFE SA offers a two-year mechanical engineering associate degree in partnership with local universities. Graduates in mechanical technician roles report estimated annual salaries ranging from 80,000 to 85,000 dollars. The full list includes eight distinct pathways.

stories.title: Predictive analytics market reaches 27.5 billion dollars
stories.summary: The global predictive analytics market reached between 21 billion and 27.5 billion dollars in 2026, growing at roughly 20 percent annually. Organizations are shifting from simple forecasting to determining specific actions, such as building retention strategies. Algorithms now routinely estimate outcomes before hospital clinics or warehouses begin daily operations.

stories.title: RIT students win Microsoft hackathon
stories.summary: Five Rochester Institute of Technology students won first place at a Microsoft hackathon in New York City. The team developed a strategy to improve trust in agentic e-commerce. They were selected from over 1,000 applications to solve a real business challenge alongside industry professionals.

stories.title: Visa rules complicate NIL earnings for international athletes
stories.summary: International student-athletes in the US face hurdles accessing NIL and revenue-sharing payments due to F-1 visa restrictions on promotional work. While legal to receive funds, the path is narrow. Violating visa regulations can lead to significant legal consequences, including the potential loss of student status.

stories.title: U.S. ranks second in global STEM index
stories.summary: The United States ranked second worldwide in the 2026 Center for Excellence in Education Index of STEM Education. The index averages performance across five international high school Olympiads. China claimed first place, achieving top finishes in all five disciplines of biology, chemistry, mathematics, informatics, and physics.

stories.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea discuss education ties
stories.summary: An Uzbek parliamentary delegation visited South Korea to discuss expanding cooperation in teacher training, student exchanges, and joint academic programs. Talks included methods to improve preschool education and foreign language instruction. Currently, 3,500 children attend kindergartens involved in the discussed educational frameworks.

stories.title: Visa barriers shift student migration patterns
stories.summary: A survey of 437 universities shows international students are increasingly choosing Asia and Europe over the US and Britain. Undergraduate numbers in the UK and US fell by 19 percent and 13 percent respectively. Processing delays and tougher screening were cited as the primary factors driving the change.

stories.title: New approaches to educator assessment
stories.summary: The State Quality Service of Education of Ukraine has discussed new frameworks for assessing educators, focusing on the transition from evaluation to professional growth. The full details of these proposed approaches are available for subscribers.

stories.title: Karolinska Institutet study supports department-based faculty training
stories.summary: A study at Karolinska Institutet suggests that department-based faculty development programmes help university teachers adopt scholarly teaching approaches. The research, published in BMC Medical Education, notes that this method addresses the difficulty of translating generic pedagogical training into actual workplace practice. Workshops are now being asked to work.

stories.title: Developing teaching careers in Canada
stories.summary: University Affairs provides guidance on building a teaching-focused career at Canadian post-secondary institutions. The full article is available for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Iran wins gold at astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: Iran's national B team secured six gold medals at the fifth Open World Astronomy Olympiad in Russia. The competition, held from November 6 to 14 in the Sirius Federal Territory, saw all six team members achieve top honours in the international scientific event.

stories.title: Ambekar Meetei wins historic boxing gold
stories.summary: Ambekar Meetei became the first Indian boxer to win gold at the Youth Olympics. His career, marked by financial hardship, follows years of training supported by his family. The win follows his progression from local competitions to the international podium.

stories.title: Maharashtra state schools chess championship begins
stories.summary: The SBI Life Maharashtra State Schools Chess Championship 2026 has started at Rustomjee Cambridge International School with 387 players. The three-day event features six FIDE-rated categories for students aged nine to seventeen. Leading seeds are currently maintaining their momentum as the tournament enters its second stage.

stories.title: Wrestlers qualify for Commonwealth Championships
stories.summary: Kajal Dhochak and Neelam Sirohi secured spots in the Indian team for the upcoming Commonwealth Wrestling Championships after winning selection trials. Kajal, a recent world championship silver medalist, qualified in the 76kg category. The event is scheduled to take place next month.

stories.title: Turkmen students earn medals in Poland
stories.summary: Students from Turkmenistan performed at the International Team Mathematics Olympiad in Katowice, Poland. Oguzhan Garlyev of the Yagshygeldi Kakayev International Oil and Gas University earned a gold medal, while two other students secured bronze. The event hosted participants from across the United Kingdom, Austria, and Poland.

stories.title: Birla Public School students win at international debate
stories.summary: Students from Birla Public School, Doha, secured honours in the Junior and Senior categories at the SAI Global Debate Competition. Forty-two schools from seven countries participated in the event, which required participants to demonstrate critical thinking and persuasive argumentation. The school has been notified of its success.

stories.title: Turkmen students win physics grand prix
stories.summary: Students from Magtymguly Turkmen State University won the Grand Prix and five medals at the World Young Physicists Olympiad in Bali. Musa Artykov took home the Grand Prix and a gold medal, while the team also secured an additional gold, two silver, and one bronze medal.

stories.title: Max Tang makes waves in and out of the pool
stories.summary: Even his weekends are likely to involve training rather than putting his feet up. “There isn’t much free time to balancing everything can definitely be challenging,” Tang shared. Yet the Kuala Lumpur teen seems to thrive on the demanding routine. For someone who once came

stories.title: Four Jackson High seniors named National Merit semifinalists
stories.summary: Four seniors at Henry M. Jackson High School have been named 2027 National Merit Scholarship semifinalists. Callia Park, Madeleine Swanson, Alyssa Webb, and Milo Bostrom were recognized for their PSAT scores, placing them among the top 1 percent of high school seniors nationwide.

stories.summary: Joy Nyokabi Karinge, PhD Anthropology Student, Co-Authors New Book! stories.title: Foundation holds scholarship exam for 3,000 students
stories.summary: The Dr Mostafa-Hazera Foundation held its seventh annual merit scholarship exam for 3,000 class eight students. The two-day test, conducted across multiple centres in Dhaka and Noakhali, evaluated students on English, Bangla, mathematics, and general knowledge to determine eligibility for upcoming stipends and certificates.

stories.title: Mysuru gets LED dome planetarium
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has inaugurated the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru, India's first LED dome facility. The government says the center will inspire scientific curiosity and help students explore the universe. The facility is intended to contribute to the country's ongoing scientific journey.

stories.title: Odisha launches robotic labs in 807 schools
stories.summary: Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has launched robotic laboratories across 807 government schools at a cost of 164.33 crore rupees. The initiative provides training in coding, AI, and 3D printing for students. The Chief Minister also introduced the Nipun App to support foundational learning in primary schools.

stories.title: An infant with a single eye socket was buried 1,600 years ago in Peru, ancient DNA reveals an extra chromosome 13
stories.summary: A burial in southern Peru has given researchers an unusual glimpse into a rare congenital condition that affected a child around 1,600 years ago. The infant, buried in a cemetery belonging to the ancient Nasca culture, had cyclopia, a severe developmental condition in which the

stories.summary: Students from Turkmenistan became prize-winners of the mathematics olympiad vestiabad.ru The full piece is for subscribers, and the headline is all that is public for now. Further details were not available in the open teaser.

stories.summary: Odisha CM launches robotic labs in 807 schools The initiative will enable students in classes 6 to 10 to receive practical training in robotics, coding, AI, machine learning and 3D printing. stories.title: Construction expo introduces teens to skilled trades
stories.summary: Junior Achievement of Southeast Michigan hosted a construction expo for high school students in Detroit. Teens practiced hammering, drywall installation, and electrical work with licensed tradespeople. Organizers noted that Michigan faces 35,000 annual skilled-trade openings, with some roles offering pay exceeding 100,000 dollars a year.

stories.title: Did you know women scientists were denied credit for groundbreaking discoveries? The practice even has a name: Matilda e
stories.summary: Scientific history is filled with discoveries that have transformed the world, but the recognition for these achievements has not always been shared equally. For generations, women scientists have contributed to groundbreaking research, developed important theories and worked alongside leading researchers, only to find their contributions

stories.title: Goa: Indian Navy Conducts Fifth Edition Of 'Sea Vigil-26' To Test Coastal Security Readiness
stories.summary: The Indian Navy is conducting the fifth edition of the pan-India coastal defence exercise 'Sea Vigil-26' from November 11 to 19, 2026. The exercise spans India's coastline and Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), focusing on coastal defence and maritime security preparedness. Visuals from Vasco, Goa, show

stories.title: Beyond textbooks and report cards: 10 life skills every child should master before stepping into high school
stories.summary: A child may know multiplication tables, remember historical dates and score well in examinations, but would they know how to manage their pocket money, handle rejection, ask for help or respond to an emergency? These are everyday situations that children eventually encounter, yet many grow

stories.title: Harvard releases AI guidance for students
stories.summary: The Harvard Graduate School of Education has launched an AI Guidance by Age Matrix to help students and teachers navigate technology in the classroom. The resource draws on over 5,000 research publications across 81 developmental areas to determine how AI might support or hinder learning at different stages.

stories.title: Five habits to reduce academic stress
stories.summary: Educational psychology suggests that academic stress often stems from disorder rather than difficulty. Researchers recommend five habits to improve learning, including establishing a fixed study time and place. A structured ninety minutes is often more effective than four hours of aimless effort for a child.

stories.title: Stanford study examines math difficulties
stories.summary: Researchers at Stanford University are investigating why some children struggle with mathematics despite intensive effort. Published in The Journal of Neuroscience, the study suggests that developmental dyscalculia may be linked to how a child's brain assesses and switches between different problem-solving methods rather than simple memorisation.

stories.title: The digital divide in the age of AI
stories.summary: As generative AI becomes integral to education, a new digital divide is emerging. The challenge for students in smaller cities is no longer just internet access, but the infrastructure and skills required to benefit from AI tools. Without inclusive access, the technology may become an academic barrier.

stories.title: Questioning AI as a civic skill
stories.summary: Educators and parents are increasingly focused on AI literacy as a tool for future career relevance. However, some argue that the current conversation misses a broader point. Preparing students for the future requires teaching them to question AI as citizens, not just as workers.

stories.title: CBSE schools in Mangalore promote sustainability
stories.summary: CBSE schools in Mangalore are encouraging students to adopt sustainable habits through everyday choices. By switching off lights, using paper carefully, and avoiding food waste, the schools aim to teach responsible living. Sustainability, the initiative suggests, does not always require large-scale environmental projects to begin.

stories.summary: District Administration print and digital media serve the top K12 leaders at virtually every school district in the U.S., helping administrators make informed decisions about best practices and research-based approaches to improve teacher quality and increase student achievement across their districts. stories.title: Stanford students push back on surveillance
stories.summary: Stanford University has ended its contract with Flock Safety following a student-led campaign against the use of automated license plate readers. Students argued that the technology could be exploited to victimise vulnerable people. The school is now working to codify safeguards for future technology use.

stories.title: The AI classroom dilemma
stories.summary: Generative AI has become a common study aid, with surveys indicating that up to 80 percent of university students use platforms like ChatGPT for coursework. While some see these tools as digital tutors, educators remain concerned about the potential impact on critical thinking and academic integrity.

stories.title: India and Pakistan to meet in U19 Asia Cup final
stories.summary: India will face Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup 2026 final on November 14 in Oman. India is chasing a record-extending ninth title, while defending champions Pakistan aim for their third. The Indian side is looking to avenge a group-stage defeat against their rivals.

stories.title: HSE University offers master's scholarships
stories.summary: The Higher School of Economics University has opened its 2026 to 2027 international olympiad for postgraduate students. The competition offers participants a chance to win tuition-free master's degree scholarships in Russia. The programme covers 128 academic fields for successful applicants from the global community.

stories.title: New civics contest offers scholarships
stories.summary: The American Cornerstone Institute has launched the Little Patriots contest for Maryland K-5 students. The programme offers scholarships of up to $100,000 for participants. Entries for the competition are due by December 15, with the finals scheduled to take place in Washington.

stories.title: UAH accepting applications for cybersecurity scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Alabama in Huntsville is accepting applications for scholarships for cybersecurity. The scholarships are available through UAH’s Center for Cybersecurity Research and Education through the CyberCorps: Scholarship for Service (SFS) program and Department of War (DOW) Cyber Service Academy (CSA). The scholarships are

stories.title: CBSE releases Class 10 board examination schedule
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has published the date sheet for the 2027 Class 10 examinations. Testing is scheduled to run from 16 February to 9 March. Students are expected to report for two-hour or three-hour sessions, depending on the subject requirements.

stories.title: CISCE announces ICSE Class 10 examination timetable
stories.summary: The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations released the 2027 ICSE Class 10 date sheet on 10 November. The notification includes the full schedule for theory papers, reporting instructions and session timings. Candidates may access the official timetable through the council portal.

stories.title: CBSE Class 12 theory examination dates confirmed
stories.summary: The CBSE has released the 2027 Class 12 date sheet, with theory examinations scheduled from 16 February to 9 April. The timetable covers subjects across Science, Commerce and Humanities streams. All examinations are set to begin at 10:30 AM.

stories.title: IIT Delhi sets JEE-Advanced date for May 2027
stories.summary: IIT Delhi will conduct the JEE-Advanced entrance exam on 23 May 2027. Only the top 2.5 lakh candidates from the JEE-Main exam are eligible to participate. The institute confirmed that students will be permitted to use a basic, non-scientific calculator during the test.

stories.title: IIT Delhi sets JEE Advanced 2027 date
stories.summary: IIT Delhi has announced that JEE Advanced 2027 will take place on May 23, 2027. The institute launched an official website for the exam, which restricts eligibility to students who first appeared for Class 12 in 2026 or 2027. The calendar is now set.

stories.title: Uttarakhand releases UTET 2026 results
stories.summary: The Uttarakhand Board of School Education has declared results for the UTET 2026 Paper 1 and Paper 2. Candidates can download scorecards and marksheets from the official website until November 25, 2026. Access requires a registration number, password, and the displayed captcha code.

stories.title: Karnataka NEET UG vacancy round results declared
stories.summary: The Karnataka Examination Authority has released final seat allotment results for the NEET UG 2026 special stray vacancy round. Of 47 medical seats available, 20 were allotted and 27 remain vacant. Successful candidates must now complete the required payment process.

stories.title: Haryana Board declares Class 12 supplementary results
stories.summary: The Board of School Education Haryana has released results for its October 2026 supplementary examinations. The academic stream recorded a 68.32 percent pass rate, while the Open School stream saw 52.10 percent of students pass. Results are available on the board website.

stories.title: Kerala announces 2027 SSLC and Plus Two dates
stories.summary: The Kerala government has scheduled its SSLC and Plus Two examinations for March 2027. More than 13 lakh students are expected to participate in the public exams, with the Class 10 assessment beginning on March 1. The state is preparing for the influx.

stories.title: AIBE 22 admit cards arriving tomorrow
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India will release admit cards for the AIBE 22 examination on November 14, 2026. The test is scheduled for November 29. Candidates must download and print the document, as it is compulsory for entry into the examination centre.

stories.title: ICSI to release CSEET October results
stories.summary: The Institute of Company Secretaries of India will declare CSEET October 2026 results on November 15 at 2 pm. The announcement will include subject-wise mark breakdowns and an e-Result-cum-Marks Statement for download. The institute has confirmed the timeline for the release.

stories.title: JKSSB releases Finance Account Assistant admit cards
stories.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir Services Selection Board has issued admit cards for the Finance Account Assistant examination scheduled for November 15, 2026. The recruitment drive aims to fill 600 vacancies. Applicants must present the document to gain entry to the hall.

stories.title: Korean labor market faces student visa hurdles
stories.summary: Only 34.3 percent of international graduates who remain in Korea secure local employment, despite filling regional labor gaps. Experts suggest the country needs policies to help graduates integrate into local communities. One student from Uzbekistan is currently navigating the postgraduation transition.

stories.title: UK student visa applications drop in October
stories.summary: UK student visa applications fell by 31 percent in October compared to the same period last year. Factors influencing the decline include university recruitment strategies, rising living costs, and changes to post-study work rights. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Governments tighten international student visa compliance
stories.summary: Governments are increasing scrutiny on study visa applications, leading to lower issuance rates in the UK, Canada, and the US. Agencies are training officers to identify false pretences, while backlogs and stricter compliance rules continue to impact student mobility across the globe.

stories.title: Australia updates graduate visa family rules
stories.summary: New rules for Temporary Graduate visas starting November 13, 2026, require eligible family members to be included in the primary application. Subsequent entry for family members is no longer permitted. The Migration Amendment Regulations 2026 aim to combine all family requests into one.

stories.title: Canada caps international student arrivals
stories.summary: Canada will limit new international student arrivals to 150,000 annually from 2027 to 2029. This target represents a decrease from the 2026 goal of 155,000 and a significant reduction from the 2025 target of 305,900. The government continues to regulate temporary resident numbers.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu allocates funds for education
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has allocated 52,920 crore rupees for education in the 2026 to 27 budget, with 8,393 crore dedicated to higher education. The funding aims to modernize infrastructure and expand AI skilling as the state pursues a knowledge-driven economy.

stories.title: Lithuania updates visa rules for Indian citizens
stories.summary: Lithuania has unveiled new visa rules for Indian citizens following a report. Access to the specific details of the policy change is currently restricted on the server. The update follows recent scrutiny of the country's visa processes.

stories.title: India simplifies visa categories and forms
stories.summary: The Indian government has reduced its main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23. Application forms have also been shortened by 65 to 70 percent. The overhaul aims to simplify travel for tourism, business, and education.

stories.title: Foreign university campuses in India see low enrollment
stories.summary: Foreign universities with Indian campuses are struggling to meet enrollment expectations. For the 2026 and 2027 academic year, 13 top-ranked institutions offered 2,730 seats across 91 programmes. Initial figures have fallen significantly short of the intended capacity.

stories.title: Canada maintains restricted student permit environment
stories.summary: Canada’s 2027 to 2029 Immigration Levels Plan keeps new international student arrivals at 150,000 per year. Students will comprise 40 percent of the 370,000 total temporary resident arrivals. The policy signals that the country does not plan to return to previous higher intake levels.

stories.title: No sandpaper distractions as Australia thump England after debutant heroics
stories.summary: No sandpaper distractions as Australia thump England after debutant heroics Amid the Sandpapergate controversy, Mahli Beardman and Mitchell Marsh shifted the spotlight back to cricket with a dominant display in Perth. Beardman's record-breaking six-wicket haul and Marsh's blistering fifty powered Australia to a seven-wicket win

stories.title: Stricter visa rules push students toward Asia and Europe
stories.summary: International students are increasingly choosing universities in Asia and continental Europe over the US and UK. Stricter visa policies and immigration regulations in traditional education hubs have made entry more difficult. Universities in Asia and Europe are now positioning themselves to capture the shifting market of students.

stories.title: FAMU students use AI to visualize DNA
stories.summary: Florida A&M University students are using Google Gemini to assist with microbiology coursework. Second-year student Natalie Henderson used the tool to map connections between DNA components, then verified the output against course materials. The summit encouraged students to use AI while maintaining their own independent thinking.

stories.title: TCS launches AI literacy initiative for schools
stories.summary: Tata Consultancy Services is rolling out a nationwide AI literacy programme for schools following a pilot at Little Angels School. The initiative aims to provide students and teachers with the skills to use AI in a positive way as the technology changes how classrooms and workplaces operate.

stories.title: Teacher integrates AI into literature classes
stories.summary: Nguyen Ngoc Anh, a teacher at Kim Xuyen High School, is incorporating AI into her literature curriculum. The initiative aims to ensure students in disadvantaged areas do not fall behind in the digital age. She was recently named one of the 100 outstanding young teachers of 2026.

stories.title: Teachers unions sign AI agreement with Anthropic
stories.summary: The American Federation of Teachers and the United Federation of Teachers have signed a binding contract with Anthropic. The agreement enforces data privacy and transparency standards for Claude for Teachers across thousands of school districts. The contract is legally enforceable.

stories.title: Artificial intelligence in the classroom

stories.title: TSC introduces dual promotion paths for teachers
stories.summary: The Teachers Service Commission has introduced two promotion pathways for public school teachers to address career stagnation. Educators may now choose between a track focused on classroom instruction or one dedicated to school leadership and administration. The framework follows a review of the 2018 career guidelines.

stories.title: TSC proposes major overhaul of teachers' promotion structure with two career paths
stories.summary: The Teachers Service Commission (TSC) is proposing a major restructuring of teachers' career progression that could change how educators advance professionally, with a new model separating classroom teaching from administrative leadership. The proposed review of the 2018 Career Progression Guidelines (CPG) seeks to address longstanding

stories.title: Cambridge report calls for teacher involvement in AI policy
stories.summary: A new Cambridge University Press and Assessment report recommends that policymakers include teachers and learners in the design and procurement of AI tools. The report argues that policy must be grounded in classroom realities. Apparently, the people using the tools are considered relevant to their implementation.

stories.title: Amity University hosts Bhutanese teachers for immersion
stories.summary: Amity University is hosting 40 teachers from Bhutan for a five-day immersion programme. The initiative aims to familiarise participants with international education standards, innovative teaching methods and the use of artificial intelligence. The programme concludes on November 16, 2026.

stories.title: UNESCO and Bayelsa government launch AI teacher training
stories.summary: UNESCO and the Bayelsa State Ministry of Education have begun a three-day training programme for master trainers. The project aims to build capacity in digital pedagogy and artificial intelligence for ICT lecturers across the state. It is funded by the European Union.

stories.title: Diocesan teachers meet for professional development
stories.summary: Catholic school teachers from the Arlington diocese gathered at Bishop O’Connell High School for a professional development day. The event included Mass, keynote addresses on student mental health and breakout sessions. The diocese holds these gatherings for all K-12 teachers every two years.

stories.title: Lighthouse Learning partners with Meru International School
stories.summary: Lighthouse Learning has announced a strategic partnership with Meru International School in Hyderabad. The collaboration aims to combine Meru's inquiry-led approach with Lighthouse Learning's technology platforms and national network. The school operates two campuses and is currently developing a third in Gopanpally.

stories.title: California teachers union seeks three-year AI pause
stories.summary: The California teachers union is calling for a three-year pause on the use of artificial intelligence in K-8 classrooms. The full details of the proposal and the union's reasoning are available to subscribers of EdSource.

stories.title: Bengaluru school faces FIR over tree pruning
stories.summary: The forest department has registered an FIR against a Bengaluru school for cutting 12 branches from two trees without permission. The school stated the pruning was a safety measure to protect students. The case was filed under the Karnataka Preservation of Trees Act.

stories.title: Bhiwandi schools consider CBSE curriculum
stories.summary: The Bhiwandi Nizampur City Municipal Corporation has proposed introducing CBSE-affiliated English-medium classes to address declining enrollment. The initiative aims to provide affordable education to families who cannot afford private school fees. The proposal will be placed before the general body for approval on November 17.

stories.title: Lighthouse Learning acquires stake in Meru International
stories.summary: Lighthouse Learning has struck a deal to acquire a stake in the Hyderabad-based Meru International School. The company, controlled by private equity firm KKR, is integrating the school into its network. The partnership focuses on academic delivery and faculty development.

stories.title: Ofsted inspections face criticism
stories.summary: Simon Jenkins writes that government regulation of state schools by Ofsted remains a fiasco. Following the 2023 death of a headteacher, the agency replaced single-word ratings with colour-coded report cards. The teaching profession continues to express significant dissatisfaction with the new grading system.

stories.title: Kenya faces administrative split in comprehensive schools
stories.summary: Kenya's comprehensive schools are struggling with an administrative disconnect between national and county governments. Early Childhood Development Education falls under county control, while primary and secondary levels are managed nationally. Teachers in the same building are currently governed by two different employment structures.

stories.title: St. Louis school board votes to close nine schools
stories.summary: The St. Louis school board has voted to close nine schools due to declining enrolment and underutilised facilities. The district is following a trend seen in many other school systems across the country. Further details are available to subscribers.

stories.title: Texas voters focus on education
stories.summary: Michelle Palmer, a candidate for the Texas state board of education, reports that voters are increasingly concerned about education policy. Issues include a voucher program diverting public funds to private schools and new social studies standards. Parents appear to have decided that their children are not to be messed with.

stories.title: Stalin criticizes scholarship scheme management
stories.summary: DMK president MK Stalin has accused the TVK government of attempting to dismantle the Annal Ambedkar Overseas Higher Education Scholarship Scheme. He claims students are facing mental distress due to withheld tuition fees. The government has not yet responded to the allegations regarding the welfare initiative.

stories.title: Mewat engineering students end hunger strike
stories.summary: Students at Mewat Engineering College have ended a 13-day hunger strike following a written assurance from the Haryana Waqf Board. The protest, which began over a month ago, concerns dilapidated buildings and faculty shortages. Students are now waiting for concrete timelines for the promised infrastructure improvements.

stories.title: Kerala plans dedicated nursing university
stories.summary: The Kerala government intends to establish a dedicated nursing university and increase nursing seats by 50 percent. Chief Minister V D Satheesan stated that the expansion would prioritize the health sector despite financial constraints. The government claims this growth will not compromise existing educational standards.

stories.title: ISB founders reflect on Hyderabad campus
stories.summary: As the Indian School of Business celebrates its 25th anniversary, founders have revealed that Delhi was their original preference for the campus. The institution eventually chose Hyderabad after rejecting a reservation proposal from Shiv Sena. The full piece is available for subscribers.

stories.title: IIT Kharagpur introduces medical degrees
stories.summary: IIT Kharagpur has become the first IIT to offer postgraduate medical programmes accredited by the National Medical Commission. Starting in the 2026 to 2027 academic year, the institute will offer MD degrees in six specialisations. The move aims to integrate medical training into the existing engineering ecosystem.
